title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. In Chapter III, 'Réseaux via découpages' (1986), Grothendieck axiomatises a 'tame topology' (topologie modérée) abstractly. The data are:
- an ordered set M of 'tame parts';
- a symmetric relation on pairs, '{X,Y} mod.' (modérée or modulaire: X and Y are in tame/compatible position), for which X∧Y and X∨Y exist;
- a distinguished subset M_f of 'closed' elements, with a closure X ↦ X̄;
- a complement X' = the largest Y with {X,Y} mod. and X∧Y = ∅.
These satisfy axioms 1)–7), with 8) on the previous page giving the frontier Fr X = X̄∧X̄'. The previous page ends by noting that for mutually modular elements one can write Boolean-ring operations X+Y, X·Y.

This page: relativisation to an element A. Fix A ∈ M and set M_A = M_{≤A} = {Y ∈ M | Y ⊂ A}, the principal down-set, with the induced order. Grothendieck declares the following:
- {X,Z} is mod. in M_A iff it is mod. in M.
- X ∈ M_A is closed in M_A iff X = X̄∧A, i.e. iff X = Z∧A for some closed Z ∈ M_f with {Z,A} mod. This is the subspace topology.

He then claims axioms 1)–7) still hold for M_A:
1) The bottom is ∅_M and the top is 1_{M_A} = A. The page writes 'X', evidently a slip for A.
2) Trivial.
3) For a mod. pair X, Y ⊂ A, the meet X∧Y and join X∨Y computed in M lie below A. Hence they are the inf and sup in M_A.
4) Relative complement. For X ∈ M_A, consider the Y ⊂ A with {X,Y} mod. and X∧Y = ∅. By definition of X' each such Y is ≤ X', and it is also ≤ A, so Y ≤ X'∧A. He asserts that X'∧A itself has the required properties, so it is the largest such Y. Hence the complement in M_A is ∁_A X = X'∧A.

The next page goes on to check that mutually modular families in M_A generate Boolean algebras compatibly with those of M. This uses {X,Y} mod. ⇒ {A∧X', A∧Y'} mod. It then checks axioms 5) and 6), the latter by describing closures in M_A.

Purpose. This is the standard check that the axiom system is stable under passage to a 'subspace'. It is needed for a theory of tame stratified spaces / 'réseaux' built by successive cutting (découpages).
errors: 1) '1_{M_A} = X' should read 1_{M_A} = A; this is a slip of the pen.

4) The proof only shows maximality. It does not justify that X'∧A is defined, which requires {X',A} mod. It also does not justify that {X, X'∧A} is mod. Both need the facts that X ≤ A implies {X,A} mod. and that mod. pairs are preserved under complement and meet. The next page partly supplies these via the Boolean algebra generated by mutually modular families.
The claim that {X,Z} is mod. in M_A iff it is mod. in M is stated as a definition or obvious. It is a choice of induced structure, not something proved.

ideas.what: Relativisation of the axiomatic tame-set structure to a principal down-set M_{≤A}, with the induced compatibility relation and the subspace closure X̄∧A
ideas.modern_name: Induced/subspace structure; principal ideal [0,a] of a lattice-like structure; definable subsets of a definable set in o-minimal structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (lattice theory; van den Dries for o-minimal tame topology)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is programmatic in Esquisse d'un programme §5 (1984); this axiomatics is unpublished.

ideas.what: Relative complement ∁_A X = X'∧A as the largest element disjoint from X and compatible with it inside A
ideas.modern_name: Relative orthocomplement in the interval [0,a] (as in orthomodular lattices / partial Boolean algebras)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical: intervals of orthomodular lattices are orthomodular (Kalmbach etc.); partial Boolean algebras (Kochen–Specker 1967)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's structure is close to an orthomodular poset or partial Boolean algebra. It has a poset with a compatibility relation ('mod.'), meets and joins defined for compatible pairs, a complement, and mutually compatible families generating Boolean algebras (next page). The relativisation here mirrors the known fact that intervals [0,a] inherit the structure, with relative complement x'∧a. The notes do not make this link, and the tame-topology literature has not exploited it.
missed.quote: considérons les Y∈M_A en position mod. p.r. à X, telles que Y∧X=∅ ... ≤ X'∧A, qui a les propriétés voulues
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only a mild curiosity. An abstract, Boolean-algebra-of-compatible-pairs axiomatics of tame topology could be compared with quantum-logic structures. It could also be compared with the lattice/Boolean-algebra approaches to o-minimal and definable sets. No new theorem is involved.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine verification that the axioms pass to the principal down-set M_{≤A} (subspace). It is of interest only as part of Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatisation of tame topology from 1986.
transcription_corrections: Every 'connexe [?]' should read 'mod.' (modérée/modulaire), consistent with the neighbouring pages.
'3) item car' should read '3) idem car'.
'1_{M_A} = X' is what is written, but A is intended.
'en position connexe [?] p.r. à X' should read 'en position mod. p.r. à X'.
Final line: 'et c'est la plus grande des leurs [?]' is more likely 'et c'est la plus grande des Y' (or 'de toutes'), OK.
